title: [AINews] Riemann Hypothesis proved...twice independently
author: swyx .ai
text: Within a few hours of each other ( timeline ), two mathematicians claimed independent proofs of the Riemann Hypothesis, the most famous open problem in mathematics ( Scientific American ). Levent Alpöge of Anthropic first made his Claude-driven proof in a note released with Lean code (1.3GB worth, ~250,000 page equivalent) rather than a full paper. Elliot Glazer confirms that the formalized statement is GRH and puts the chance of a Lean bug well under 1%. So if it finishes compiling with no extra axioms, it is probably correct, and no human will ever have read all of it… …prompting Alessandro Masullo to release his 940 page, 100% human , work in progress proof he had been working on for the last 12 years (and had been undergoing secret manual review and revision per Kevin Hartnett ). This is the third in the trilogy of frontier math breakthroughs, following from the Navier Stokes solutions and the Quasi-Riemann bounding, but it doesn’t feel over. OpenAI's September Navier-Stokes claim is still the cautionary tale: critics argued that its Lean proof did not match the natural-language result. Both AI-claimed Millennium Prize results will take years to verify. Apart from the incredible accomplishment of the most famous problem in mathematics, one cannot miss the contrast that the AI-written solution is probably correct but incomprehensible , and the other solution is probably technically incorrect but understandable . Sponsored by Agentfield.AI Open models are ready. Most coding harnesses aren’t. On DeepSWE, CodeAF finished #1 of ten on the same open model, ahead of Claude Code, at the lowest cost per fix. Try CodeAF ! As Levent eloquently put it: “ Claude far outpaced me near the finish line . No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.” This also ties into other AI themes we’ve covered on the podcast and on this newsletter: The nature of Slop : Levent says “ I am presenting the world with a complete argument before having mastered a massive neighbourhood around its mathematics. It being obviously inappropriate to attempt to post some massive unreadable travesty of "slop", I decided to only present Lean . ” One of the key tenets of the No Slop Manifesto is that you should understand what you ship (“ Slop is when we put less effort into producing something than we ask the consumer to spend understanding it. ”). And yet, this giant pile of Lean is verifiably correct and is incredibly significant in human history. Should we have delayed its release by a decade simply because we didn’t understand every single bit of it? Weak to Strong alignment : the typical experience of using agents is Strong to Weak - we are general intelligences guiding not-as-smart AI to do things we know how to do well. We also often expect AI to automate most work “within distribution”, and expect it to run into more trouble at the limits of capability where the “centaur” pattern of human-AI-collaboration is required. Levent’s lived experience is the opposite - collaborating with Claude only in the early stages and then leaving him far behind with the critical parts involving automorphic forms on higher-rank groups. We are starting to need Weak to Strong alignment — the open ended domain of controlling AI smarter than us. title: The War Against Slop and an Emerging Weapon to Fight it: Formal Verification
author: Richard MacManus
text: The word of the year in the AI industry over 2026 has been “slop” — meaning low-quality output from a large language model. And with so much code being AI-generated now, avoiding slop has become a daily concern for software engineers. So how to do that? One way is to use formal verification systems , which use mathematical proofs and logic to verify the correctness of software or hardware. With AI’s growing prowess at solving math problems , there’s now a number of AI companies offering formal verification systems. They include Harmonic , Theorem , Axiom Math , and a new entrant called &Truth (pronounced ‘and truth’). In this article we’ll look at some of the approaches these companies are taking. How formal verification is used in software and AI today In order to better understand the landscape of formal verification systems, we spoke to one of its leading proponents: Clark Barrett , &Truth’s co-founder and co-CEO. He’s also Corbel Professor (Research) of Computer Science at Stanford and was the co-creator of cvc5 , a popular automated reasoning engine used in formal verification. Without getting too in the weeds, cvc5 is what’s called a “solver” for satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) , which Barrett says is widely used in companies like Amazon. For instance, cvc5 is used for specification analysis and test generation in Kiro , Amazon’s agentic development environment. “It's been fun to see my tools go from a good idea in the lab to cvc5 is now called billions of times a day in production pipelines at Amazon,” Barrett told us. Via a 2022 paper about cvc5 co-authored by Clark Barrett. When AI coding agent companies talk about “verifying” their work, it typically means agents running tests, critiquing their own output, or having another AI model judge it. So I asked Barrett how far short of real verification does that fall? “The main difference is really just, how do you know when you're done,” he replied. “So if you're testing, patching, scanning — using all these existing tools — they're quite good. I mean, they find a ton of problems. They raise those issues. But you're never quite sure, did I find all of them [the issues] or is there one more lurking there that my tool can't find?” &Atlas, the first tool of &Truth; it’s “a map of the world’s open-source code, starting with code written in the C programming language.” Lean’s role in formal verification &Truth builds on Lean , an open-source programming language and proof assistant . The company combines AI with automated reasoning techniques to construct proofs that Lean can check. Lean is a language used by frontier models to solve all manner of supremely difficult math problems . For instance, just this week GPT-6.2 Astra produced what Vals believes is “the first Lean proof of Smoktunowicz’s Gap Theorem.” Vals added that Anthropic also used Lean to formalize Fermat’s Last Theorem, a project of 13 million lines. The latest big math news is a report that Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims he used Claude to prove the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis — and he posted the proof in Lean . Example of Lean code; via Lean project website &Truth is building what it calls a “verification machine” on top of the Lean framework, with the ambition of reading code “in any language, proving whether it satisfies precisely stated requirements , and enabling humans to trust it without having to understand every line.” “What Lean does is it just checks that you didn't make a mistake,” explained Barrett. “So you can think of it as a very sophisticated checker for mathematics.” This has implications for model training too. Axiom Math uses formal verification to provide correctness feedback for training its mathematical reasoning systems, with proof attempts helping improve future models. title: Show HN: OpenComputer – an open source alternative to Devin
author: iacguy
text: Hi HN! Utpal here, I'm one of the founders of OpenComputer. OpenComputer is an open source cloud coding agent for teams that can run in your own cloud account (AWS, GCP, Azure). We run the agent harness and the sandbox on the same durable VM (architecture in the docs [1]). First commit lands in 24s; the alternatives we benchmarked took 53-72s (benchmarks below [2]). Two other choices: - One VM per team, scalable horizontally. Sessions are isolated in git worktrees. - Session files are backed up to a repo after every turn, so any session can resume on another VM. We noticed that past ~640 session-hours a month, one always-on 4 vCPU VM is cheaper than per-session E2B sandboxes, for example. So at scale, this setup would not only be faster than current SOTA coding agents, but also more cost-efficient. Feel free to try via cloud for free [4] or self host. We would love any and all feedback, and happy to answer any questions! Full demo below [3]. [1]: https://docs.opencomputer.dev/getting-started/architecture [2]: https://opencomputer.dev/blog/cloud-agents-as-fast-as-local/ [3]: https://x.com/IgorZIJ/status/2121309785882591711 [4]: https://app.opencomputer.dev

title: Ask HN: I have been unemployed for 2y. 15 years of experience, US. What to do?
author: LetThingsBeDiff
text: I'm Senior software engineer in the US (DMV area), with 15y of experience. Worked for Fortune 50+ company and bunch of mid-size companies.
